mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, keep the signed subtraction order on both sides (e.g., (A - B) = (C - D)), never convert to absolute values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence states that one difference equals another difference.
mathgap.example: Treating (A - B) = (C - D) as |A - B| = |C - D| (using absolute values).

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable’s numeric value becomes known, immediately substitute it into every pending equation to simplify and propagate constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After any direct count or solved equation yields a concrete number for a variable.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known variable unchanged in later equations, e.g., not substituting E = 5 into E - C = 4.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, i.e., after applying all earlier statements and transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a ‘more/fewer’ or ‘difference between’ statement that appears after previous information.
mathgap.example: Evaluating ‘A has 3 more than B’ with B’s initial count, ignoring a prior transfer that changed B’s count.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal set of variables and equations that are directly or indirectly connected to the queried person, and ignore unrelated parts of the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem asks for a specific individual’s count.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of 22 variables when only Shawn’s count is required, leading to unnecessary work.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique capitalized token as a separate variable, even if two names differ by only a single letter.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a new name appears in the text.
mathgap.example: Assuming ‘Ann’ and ‘Anne’ refer to the same variable.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: Interpret phrases like “the difference between the number of X that A and B have” as the signed subtraction A - B, preserving the order of the names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing a sentence that mentions “the difference between … and …”.
mathgap.example: Interpreting “the difference between A and B” as B - A instead of A - B.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Translate “A has K more (fewer) items than B” into the signed equation A - B = K (or A - B = ‑K for ‘fewer’).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparative statement using ‘more’ or ‘fewer’.
mathgap.example: Translating ‘A has 3 fewer than B’ to A - B = 3 instead of A - B = ‑3.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says “X has N items”, assign X = N at that point, overwriting any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count sentence appears.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a later ‘X has N’ statement and keeping an earlier value for X.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application (Bidirectional)
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement ‘X gives K items to Y’ appears, immediately subtract K from X and add K to Y, updating both variables for all subsequent statements; do not treat the transfer as a static equality or ignore it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer sentence is encountered in the narrative.
mathgap.example: Treating ‘Maudie gives 3 raspberries to Pamela’ as only decreasing Maudie's count while leaving Pamela unchanged, or ignoring the transfer entirely.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses which side of the equation receives the positive offset, often writing A - B = ‑K instead of A - B = K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that ‘A has K more than B’ means A - B = K; keep the sign positive for the ‘more’ case.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign when equating two differences, assuming the magnitude alone matters.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the signed subtraction order on both sides of a difference equality; do not apply absolute value.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model either skips applying a transfer or applies it after later statements, breaking the intended temporal dependencies.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, updating both donor and recipient counts for all subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes a direct count is immutable, even when later statements overwrite it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a later direct‑count sentence appears, overwrite the previous value for that variable.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model incorrectly multiplies counts when a statement only adds a fixed amount, confusing ‘more’ with a factor.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret ‘has K more than’ as addition/subtraction, not multiplication; only multiply when the language explicitly indicates scaling.
